D.treatment: reported GenAI use across multiple research stages
D.comparison: no reported use across multiple stages

O.outcome_detail: self-reported use of GenAI across the research process

cells.quote: Nearly all participants (27 out of 28) reported using GenAI across multiple stages of the research process.
cells.note: This is a qualitative focus-group report of use prevalence, not an efficacy comparison.

D.treatment: GenAI as a supportive research assistant with human oversight
D.comparison: GenAI as a substitute for core intellectual work

O.outcome_detail: perceived role of GenAI in research

cells.quote: Overall, GenAI was primarily positioned as a supportive and efficiency-enhancing research assistant rather than a substitute for core intellectual work, with human oversight consistently retained.
cells.note: The study reports a qualitative positioning contrast rather than a measured treatment effect.

O.outcome_detail: association between polygenic score for educational attainment and educational achievement

cells.quote: In the between-family analysis, the regression coef ﬁcient in the association of educational achievement on PGS did not differ between the SES groups ( Δ−2LL = 2.3, Δdf = 3, p = 0.517), which means that the strength of the effect of genetic variants related to educational attainment in predicting EA in children did not differ between SES groups.
cells.note: The non-significant result is coded as ns because no equivalence test or adequate-power claim is reported.
